clue.text: Not a bad match, but it's rightly ridiculed

definitions.meaning: a contest that is even, a fair contest between sides
a legitimate target for mockery or attack

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both an evenly matched contest and a person who deserves to be mocked.

clue.text: Wrinkle familiar to anti-mink-farm protesters?

definitions.meaning: a crease or line on the brow
split in two, a dispute over pelts, the kind of quarrel such campaigners know well

explanation.surface: A frown line that animal-rights campaigners against mink farms know well.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the second half as FUR ROW: a row (quarrel) about fur, which anti-mink-farm protesters are always having.
explanation.definitionFit: A furrow is a deep line or crease, as on a worried forehead.

clue.text: Formally ask popular sextet to take note

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
VI is six in Roman numerals
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A request to a popular group of six musicians to learn a note.
explanation.definitionFit: To invite someone is to request their presence, typically in a formal way.

clue.text: Maybe a feature some Bangor geographers study

indicators.note: only some of the letters of these two words are used, a run across the gap between them

explanation.surface: Students of geography at Bangor, a Welsh university town, might study a landscape feature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' signals a run of letters inside 'Bangor geographers'; 'study' finishes the surface. Bangor is a university town in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: A ravine is one example of a landscape feature, hence 'Maybe'.

clue.text: Order fellow worker to come round also

indicators.note: the colleague word surrounds the other piece, coming round it

parts.note: a mate is a workmate or colleague
and means also, in addition

explanation.surface: Telling a colleague to visit as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fellow worker' is one piece, a workmate; 'to come round' wraps it around the word for 'also'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandate is an official order or commission to act.

clue.text: Religious belief set him apart

indicators.note: the letters of these words are broken up and set out afresh

explanation.surface: His faith marked him out from others.
explanation.definitionFit: Theism is belief in a god or gods.

clue.text: Whisky is difficult to consume in quantity

parts.note: hard means difficult
to stuff yourself is to eat greedily

explanation.surface: Whisky being hard to drink much of.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is slang for strong spirits such as whisky.

clue.text: Investors may use it to finance a hobby

definitions.text: Investors may use it to finance
definitions.meaning: the return paid on capital, which savers can live on
a pastime or pursuit one enjoys

explanation.surface: Financiers putting money into a pastime.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both money earned on a loan or deposit and a leisure activity.

clue.text: Fellow and I embrace divers

parts.note: a fellow is a man
to fold someone in your arms is to embrace them

explanation.surface: A man and the speaker hugging some people who dive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divers' is not people underwater but the old adjective meaning various or several.
explanation.definitionFit: Divers is an archaic word for many and various, which is what manifold means.

clue.text: Common cleric constantly in pain

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: rend means tear, the cause of heart-rending pain
ever means always

explanation.surface: A churchman who is forever suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Common' points to the everyday title of a clergyman; 'in' places the word for 'constantly' within a word for tearing pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverend is the ordinary title of a member of the clergy.

clue.text: French monk goes to Prince William's school

parts.note: Br is short for Brother, title of a monk
Prince William went to Eton College

explanation.surface: A monk sends a royal to his old public school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' is not the nationality as a whole but the regional sense: a Breton comes from Brittany in France.
explanation.definitionFit: A Breton is a native of Brittany, a region of France.

clue.text: Bitter about a man

parts.note: bitter is a type of beer
c is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A grumpy man, or a pint about one.
explanation.definitionFit: Alec is a man's name.

clue.text: Alert snooker players fix their gaze there

definitions.text: snooker players fix their gaze there
definitions.meaning: where a cue sportsman keeps his eye, on the object struck

explanation.surface: Snooker players stay alert by watching where they are aiming.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means quick-witted, and literally names where a player looks.

clue.text: Typical finishing stroke

parts.note: Typical is read as typographical: the small line that ends a stroke of a printed letter

explanation.definitionFit: A serif is the little cross-line finishing a stroke of a letter in some typefaces.

clue.text: A bishop having to live in a French monastery

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to be is to exist or live

explanation.surface: A bishop who must reside in a French religious house.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbé is a French cleric, the sort of churchman found in a French monastery.

clue.text: Brave people who've been shoeless in the mine?

definitions.meaning: a North American tribe whose warriors were called braves

definitions.text: who've been shoeless in the mine?
definitions.meaning: miners going barefoot underground would end up with coal-dirtied soles

explanation.surface: Courageous folk who went barefoot in the pit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brave' is a noun: a Native American warrior. The second reading is a joke about bare feet blackened by coal dust.
explanation.definitionFit: The Blackfeet are a Native American people of the northern Plains.

clue.text: Advocates making UNESCO take money

indicators.note: the letters of the agency's name are used to make something new

parts.note: L stands for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Lawyers creating a UN agency that is paid.
explanation.definitionFit: Counsel are barristers, lawyers who plead in court.

clue.text: Wanton vandals think it's wonderful

parts.note: the word for wrecking things is also British slang for marvellous, so vandals would approve

explanation.definitionFit: In British slang the word means excellent, and literally means breaking things to pieces.

clue.text: Antagonise Elaine at work

indicators.note: the letters are put to work, rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: Upsetting a colleague named Elaine in the office.
explanation.definitionFit: To alienate someone is to make them hostile or estranged.

clue.text: Many a large, fat duck

parts.note: M is a thousand in Roman numerals, so many
L is the clothing abbreviation for large
lard is pig fat

explanation.surface: A great many plump ducks.
explanation.definitionFit: The mallard is the common wild duck.

clue.text: State benefit given by Clinton's adversary

definitions.meaning: unemployment pay from the government, in British usage
Bob ..., the Republican who ran against Bill Clinton in 1996

explanation.surface: Welfare handed out by a president's rival.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain the word means unemployment benefit, and it is also the surname of Clinton's 1996 opponent.

clue.text: It offers food containing calcium and iron

parts.note: Ca is the chemical symbol for calcium
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: A diet with minerals in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A café is a place serving snacks and meals.

clue.text: Lower-class fare

definitions.meaning: the common people, as in the lower house of Parliament
food provisions, especially shared rations at a college

explanation.surface: Food for the lower orders.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the ordinary people and daily rations of food.

clue.text: Man in the middle has to be consistent

indicators.note: the pronoun goes inside the other piece

parts.note: the core is the centre
he is a male pronoun, a man

explanation.surface: A man at the centre must be reliable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places the pronoun for 'Man' within the word for 'the middle'; 'has to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To cohere is to hang together logically, to be consistent.

clue.text: "Oh, Sleep!" it is a — thing." (Coleridge)

parts.note: a gap in a line from The Rime of the Ancient Mariner: sleep is beloved from pole to pole

explanation.definitionFit: The Ancient Mariner calls sleep a soft, kindly thing beloved of all.

clue.text: Small vegetable of glossy appearance

parts.note: a leek is a vegetable

explanation.surface: A little vegetable with a shiny look.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleek describes something smooth and shiny.

clue.text: Rock a shade of yellowish green

indicators.note: the colour named second comes first in the word

parts.note: lime is a yellowish-green colour
stone is a pale grey-beige colour

explanation.surface: A stone tinted a particular lime colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Limestone is a sedimentary rock made largely of calcium carbonate.

clue.text: Son shut up when exhausted

parts.note: pent means confined, as in pent-up

explanation.surface: A son is confined when worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: Spent means used up, tired out.

clue.text: Egghead in unsuitable location gets huffish

indicators.note: the letter is located inside the other word

parts.note: inapt means unsuitable
the head, or first letter, of egg

explanation.surface: An intellectual in the wrong place grows sulky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egghead' is not an intellectual but the first letter of 'egg'; 'in' puts it inside INAPT.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a pet is to be in a sulk, peevish.

clue.text: Adores to dine on a small settee

parts.note: loves means adores
to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: Someone who loves eating on a little sofa.
explanation.definitionFit: A loveseat is a sofa for two people.

clue.text: Company demands time to put in estimate

indicators.note: the abbreviation is placed inside the other word

parts.note: a guess is an estimate

explanation.surface: A firm requires a time estimate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to put in' puts T inside GUESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Company can mean visitors, as in 'we have company'.

clue.text: In a way, fresh water is the first of essentials

indicators.note: the letters are made fresh, put in a new order
only the opening letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: Fresh water is the first essential of life.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means so to speak, in a manner of speaking.
